summary:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive website that tells the stories of NASA's most famous space explorers for school-age space enthusiasts.

Our website features Spirit, Opportunity, the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Curiosity, and Perseverance. For each machine, we created an engaging story, a video, a timeline of its mission, real photos, its location map, and its most important achievements.

Our project addresses the challenge by turning complex space hardware into simple, visual stories that kids can explore and enjoy. From rovers that finished their missions on Mars and the Moon to probes still working today, students can discover how each machine worked and what science it made possible.

We also added a final quiz to test what students learned in a fun way. Our project is important because it keeps the legacy of these missions alive and inspires the next generation to love space, science, and engineering.
details:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten is not just a website. It is a time machine that takes school-age explorers on a journey across the Solar System.

What does it do and how does it work? The visitor begins the adventure and chooses a hero: Spirit, Opportunity, the Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle, Curiosity, or Perseverance. Each hero has its own world. Inside, you will find a powerful story told like a movie, a video that brings the mission to life, an interactive timeline from launch to last signal, real NASA photos, a live map showing exactly where the machine is on the Moon or Mars, and a wall of its greatest achievements. The journey ends with an exciting quiz where the explorer proves what they learned and becomes a certified space explorer.

What are the benefits and intended impact? We turned cold hardware and difficult science into emotional, unforgettable stories. Kids do not just read about rovers, they feel with them, they celebrate their discoveries, and they cry when a mission ends. Our goal is to keep the legacy of these forgotten heroes alive and to ignite a new generation of scientists, engineers, and dreamers who will build the next mission to Mars.

What tools did we use? We built the website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to create a fast, colorful, and mobile-friendly experience. We used real NASA images, videos, and public mission data to make every detail authentic and trusted.

How is it creative? We did not make a report, we made a story universe. Each rover is a character with a personality, a mission, a struggle, and a legacy. The mix of storytelling, timeline, map, real photos, video, and quiz turns learning into an adventure that kids want to finish.

What factors did our team consider? We designed everything for children first: simple language, big visuals, easy navigation, real information from trusted sources, and a design that works beautifully on phone and computer for every student, everywhere.
